questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Given by an Equation in Slope-Intercept Form
questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=2x-5$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=2x-5$ passes through the points $A(0,-5)$ and $B(1,-3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -5 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -5 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(5,0)$ and ${B}^{′}(4,2).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =\frac{2-0}{4-5}(x-5) \\ y & =-2(x-5) \\ y & =-2x+10 \\ 2x+y-10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=4x-1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=4x-1$ passes through the points $Q(0,-1)$ and $R(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $Q$ and $R$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -10 \\ -2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${Q}^{′}(3,-2)$ and ${R}^{′}(-10,6).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${Q}^{′}$ and ${R}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-2) & =\frac{6-(-2)}{-10-3}(x-3) \\ y+2 & =-\frac{8}{13}(x-3) \\ 13y+26 & =-8x+24 \\ 8x+13y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $x=1$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $x=1$ passes through the points $J(1,0)$ and $K(1,1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $J$ and $K$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${J}^{′}(2,1)$ and ${K}^{′}(0,4).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${J}^{′}$ and ${K}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{4-1}{0-2}(x-2) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{3}{2}(x-2) \\ 2y-2 & =-3x+6 \\ 3x+2y-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=3x+5$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=-40.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=3x+5$ passes through the points $A(0,5)$ and $B(1,8)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 5 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & -16 \\ 5 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(-10,5)$ and ${B}^{′}(-16,12).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-5 & =\frac{12-5}{-16-(-10)}(x-(-10)) \\ y-5 & =-\frac{7}{6}(x+10)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-5 & =-\frac{7}{6}(x+10) \\ 6y-30 & =-7x-70 \\ 7x+6y & =-40\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $x=4$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $x=4$ passes through the points $G(4,0)$ and $H(4,1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $G$ and $H$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 & 10 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${G}^{′}(12,4)$ and ${H}^{′}(10,6).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${G}^{′}$ and ${H}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =\frac{6-4}{10-12}(x-12) \\ y-4 & =-1(x-12)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-4 & =-x+12 \\ x+y & =16\end{aligned}
$$
